subject: Operator witnessing schedule & staged evidence bundle — draft MSA/OrderForm exhibits
messages:
From: Aaron Drake <aaron.drake@meditrust.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Dawn Li <dawn.li@meditrust.com>
Date: 2027-05-16T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Operator witnessing schedule & evidence bundle — Redwood Private deployment

Hi Marissa / Lauren,

Thanks for taking time yesterday. Procurement legal asked me to capture what we think we need so your legal/product teams can propose concrete exhibit language. High level: Meditrust needs a staged evidence bundle plus an operator-witnessing window to validate the on-prem snapshot and key custody process before signing the Order Form.

What we want to cover (initial ask):
- Witnessing: 1 day remote witnessing followed by an optional on-site 4 hour notarized witness (if required by our compliance).
- Evidence bundle: sealed snapshot hash, operator runbook excerpt, HSM key custody attestation, signed witness statement, and a short acceptance test run.
- License scope clarity: we need explicit language that the snapshot export is read-only for verification and not a transfer of the model.
- Audit window: proposed 90-day retention for evidence artifacts in the event of a later audit.

I've attached our draft MSA redlines and a short evidence checklist. Can Redwood propose exhibit text (or a few alternative clauses) for: (a) Exhibit D — Operator Witnessing; (b) Exhibit H — Evidence Staging; and (c) Section 4 (License Scope) to be safe for health-data workloads.

Next steps: can we get a proposed text and an internal runbook owner who will perform the witnessing by next Tuesday (2027-05-18)? Procurement wants to lock the orderform language before vendor evaluation week.

Appreciate it,
Aaron

--
Aaron Drake
Director, Infrastructure & Security
MediTrust Health

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Drake <aaron.drake@meditrust.com>, Dawn Li <dawn.li@meditrust.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, david_kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-16T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Operator witnessing schedule & evidence bundle — Redwood Private deployment

Aaron / Dawn — thanks for outlining this clearly. Looping in Lauren and Tessa from Legal and David from Product so we can provide both legal text and operational runbook clarity.

Quick answers and an initial proposal:
- Witnessing options: we can support (1) remote witnessed session via Zoom with screen-share of the snapshot hash and HSM attestation, (2) remote session + notarized witness statement captured on-site by a Meditrust-approved notary for the on-site option.
- Evidence bundle: we can deliver the following packaged artifacts during the witnessing window: snapshot-hash.txt (SHA256), operator-runbook-excerpt.pdf (redacted), hsm-attestation.pdf (HSM log excerpt), witness-statement-template.docx.
- License scope language: proposed insertion for Section 4.2 (License — Temporary Snapshot for Verification): "Customer may request a read-only snapshot export solely for the purpose of operator witnessing and verification. Exported artifacts shall not constitute a transfer of Model IP or rights; Redwood retains all model ownership and usage rights."

Attached: operator-witness-runbook_v1.pdf (operational steps we will run during the session) and a suggested Exhibit text stub (see redlines_MSA_v3.docx).

Questions for Meditrust:
1) Does your compliance team require our engineer to be physically present for notarization, or is a notarized Meditrust witness acceptable?
2) For HSM logs, do you need full logs or a certified excerpt hashed into the evidence bundle? We prefer certified excerpts (minimize data exposure).

We can own the remote session and provide David as runbook lead. Proposed dates: 2027-05-20 AM for a dry-run and 2027-05-24 for the witnessing window. If those work I will send calendar invites and a runsheet.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Solutions — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Dawn Li <dawn.li@meditrust.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aaron Drake <aaron.drake@meditrust.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-16T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Operator witnessing schedule & evidence bundle — Redwood Private deployment

Marissa — appreciate the quick reply. A few clarifications from our side after an initial compliance pass: 

- Notarization: our baseline requires a notarized witness statement tied to the operator identity unless we accept a third-party witness (audit firm). If Redwood's engineer signs the witness statement and a Meditrust notary notarizes it, that is acceptable.
- HSM attestation: we prefer a certified excerpt plus a signed statement from the operator noting the key ID(s) and that key material was not exported. We will not accept unfiltered logs.
- License language: your draft is good but procurement asked for an explicit non-exclusivity carveout — i.e., "Export and verification rights are limited to the explicit scope of this Order Form and do not grant rights to redistribute or re-host the Model."

Also, our security team wants to add an acceptance test step during the witness: run a small, deterministic query set (provided by us) and capture response hashes to demonstrate parity with the hosted baseline. This should be added to Exhibit H.

I attached a short annotated checklist; we expect Redwood to populate the runbook with the exact command line steps (David, can you confirm?) and to provide the final witness-statement template for our legal to review.

Thanks — Dawn

--
Dawn Li
Senior Compliance Manager
MediTrust Health
+dawn.li@meditrust.com
From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Drake <aaron.drake@meditrust.com>, Dawn Li <dawn.li@meditrust.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, david_kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-17T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Operator witnessing schedule & evidence bundle — Redwood Private deployment

Aaron / Dawn — legal here. Thanks for the useful specifics; we've reviewed and have three targeted redlines and a coordination plan to keep the contract lean while meeting Meditrust's compliance requirements.

1) Exhibit D (Operator Witnessing): add a short paragraph that the witness-statement will be signed by the operator and notarized by Customer as an accepted form; Redwood to provide a witness-statement template in advance. We will not accept language that requires Redwood personnel to surrender private keys.

2) Exhibit H (Evidence Staging & Acceptance): include the deterministic query acceptance test idea, limited to a maximum of 25 queries and pre-shared test vectors. Test output hashing is acceptable for proof-of-parity.

3) Section 4.2 (License — Snapshot): alternate proposed clause: "Redwood grants Customer a time-limited, revocable, read-only access to exported snapshot artifacts solely to validate operational controls and acceptance tests described in Exhibit H. All Model IP and derivative rights remain solely with Redwood. Customer may not use exported artifacts to train, fine-tune, or create derivative models."

Operational asks: Marissa / David — please confirm: (a) the exact command lines for the acceptance test; (b) who will be the named engineer (include contact email) who will attend the remote witness; (c) final witness-statement template by COB 2027-05-18 so Customer legal can review.

If those are in place we can accept the redlined MSA with the three exhibits added as Order Form attachments. I'll populate the redlines and share a clean exhibit draft in the Drive link.

Lauren Bishop
General Counsel (Contracts)
Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
